status: Customer Authority now has a bounded native customer-access grant: a source-bound request command, an independently reviewed approve/reject command, a revoke command, and Company/branch/department-scoped workspace/detail reads with immutable event and read-audit history. The owner also has an owner-local HTTP router, a strict Next transport, configured workspace/detail/command cutover, purchase preflight, and fail-closed native configuration. The crate is registered in the root Cargo workspace by the integrating session. The owner remains partial overall: shared composition mounting, invitations/enrollment, portal support, identity changes, duplicate review, attachments and browser acceptance remain open.

scope.workflowBoundary: The qualified slice is the source-bound customer access grant used by the customer access review list/detail and its request/approve/reject/revoke commands. Customer identity changes, duplicate review/merge, portal invitations/resend/enrollment, portal support requests/responses/closures, portal attachments, customer directory/profile summaries and every other Customer Authority workflow remain retained TypeScript.
scope.domain: Current actor policy (commerce.read, commerce.sales, commerce.approve, selected-context expiry), exact Company and optional branch/department scope, source order identity/version/kind/state validation (Sales/quote confirmed, converted, partially fulfilled or fulfilled), a 90-day expiry window, lower-cased bounded email, bounded reason/order/id shapes, independent-approval separation, requester-or-manager revocation, CAS expected versions, pending/approved decision states, immutable action names and exact receipt/row/source/event/read projections.
scope.application: One request_access use case authorizes sales+read before any source read, validates input and replay, locks order facts in the owning transaction, rejects foreign scope/stale version/ineligible kind/state before commit, and returns the persisted receipt. One change_access use case authorizes sales+read, replays by key, validates the scoped binding and current order facts, rejects self-approval and inactive/ineligible reviewers, applies rejection/approval source guards, then commits one CAS decision. access_workspace and access_detail validate every owner row and bound rows/sources/events/reads before presentation.
scope.adapters: Read/write SQL is Customer Authority-owned (`customer_access_bindings`, `customer_access_events`, `customer_access_reads`, `customer_access_identities`, `customer_portal_invitations` and `customer_portal_invitation_events`) plus read-only projections of the existing Commerce order header, Finance party display name and IAM/HR reviewer eligibility already used by the retained access reader. No Commerce, Finance, IAM, HR, Support or portal row is mutated. The caller's serializable Holding transaction is required; no transaction is opened, committed or retried here.
scope.http: Owner-local GET/POST /api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/customer-access and GET/POST /api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/customer-access/{binding_id}. Exact registered Host/Holding targets and HTTPS origins, strict idempotency-key/Content-Type/JSON body validation, bounded bodies, duplicate/unknown query rejection, private/no-store and no-referrer/nosniff responses, and bounded BusinessError status mapping. The composition backend receives transport facts only and must supply the normal Account session, current Company/branch/department scope, purchase admission and serializable owner unit.
scope.transport: ERPX_NATIVE_CUSTOMER_ACCESS_CONFIG is strictly validated: loopback-only private base, reserved ports 3000/3001/3100/3101/3103/8080 plus 5432/5433/5435 and 3200-3299 excluded, exact HTTPS Holding origins, unique hosts/slugs, 250..30000 ms timeout, bounded cookie/context/workspace headers, exact command bodies, exact workspace/detail/receipt shapes, Company/scope coherence, unique ordered rows/events, and a 2 MiB response bound. A configured failure never falls back to the retained reader or command.
scope.ssr: The customer access review list/detail and the feature-sales /customer-access GET/POST route use the native workspace/detail/commands when ERPX_NATIVE_CUSTOMER_ACCESS_CONFIG is present. An unset configuration retains customerAccessWorkspace/customerAccessHistory/requestCustomerAccess/changeCustomerAccess. Once configured, a malformed or failed native read/command is surfaced through the existing page/route error policy rather than silently replaced. The retained invitation/history merge, identity/duplicate review tabs and portal support actions remain in place.
scope.purchaseAndIdentity: The Next cutover keeps the retained requireCustomerAccessPurchasedRead and customerAccessPurchaseControls preflight and enforces new-work versus settle-existing capability for request/approve versus reject/revoke. This is a preflight, not an atomic owner unit; the composition backend must repeat current IAM, selected scope, feature release and purchase admission inside its own serializable owner transaction.
scope.notClaimed: No browser journey, authenticated page render, shared composition mount, root workspace membership, catalogue acceptance qualification, invitation/enrollment/portal support/identity/duplicate/attachment effect, job, staging, private production or Cloudflare verification.
